analysis: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is a metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency in the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase. This enzyme is crucial for converting the amino acid phenylalanine into tyrosine. When phenylalanine hydroxylase is deficient, phenylalanine accumulates in the body, leading to the symptoms associated with PKU. The enhanced information aligns with standard medical knowledge, confirming that phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency is the cause of PKU. Other enzymes listed, such as tyrosine transaminase and tyrosine hydroxylase, are involved in different metabolic pathways and do not cause PKU.
